excerpt: Misfits Market delivers discounted 'imperfect' and surplus groceries across the US. How it works, acquisitions, funding and alternatives.
content:
Misfits Market is a US online grocery service built around food that traditional retailers turn down: fruit and vegetables with cosmetic flaws, surplus stock and odd sizes, as well as meat, dairy, pantry goods and its own Odds and Ends brand of rescued items such as bacon ends. Abhi Ramesh started it in Philadelphia in 2018, and it now delivers across much of the US. A June 2025 report by WPVI (6abc) said shoppers can save as much as 30% to 50% compared with traditional stores. Its mission statement is about building a better food system by fighting food waste and supporting sustainable farming.

Customers shop during a weekly window; Misfits Market starts the cart with suggested items to help meet the order minimum, and you are charged for what is in the cart when the window closes. A Flex Plan lets customers order only when they choose. Its FAQ mentions an $8.99 alcohol service fee for wine orders but does not list the order minimum or delivery fee on that page.

In 2021 Misfits Market raised a $200 million Series C led by Accel and D1 Capital, which valued it at more than $1 billion and brought total funding to $301 million, according to TechCrunch. In 2022 it bought its rival Imperfect Foods. In May 2025 it acquired The Rounds, a delivery startup that had raised $66 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and First Round Capital; TechCrunch reported that the deal brought partnerships with apartment operators such as AvalonBay, Greystar and Related, and quoted Ramesh saying the market is ripe for consolidation.

Misfits Market only delivers in the US, and the exact delivery area depends on your ZIP code.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
